rows.en:
But... even so, the flame went out.
Just before it touched the painting.
However you looked at it, the only explanation was that the painting itself was somehow putting it out.
Everyone got so creeped out that they decided not to try any more.
But they couldn't just leave it be, either, could they?{p}

Tore it up... you say?
How can you say something so brutal?
Do you really like paintings?
Or were you just playing along with me?
Did you lie to me?
I hate liars!{p}

......No, that's not it, is it?
{a}{f:|}, you're not that careless a person.
I can tell.
You were only making a little joke, weren't you?
I understand.
But you see, I hate tasteless jokes just as much as I hate being lied to.

I'll forgive you because it's you, {a}{f:|}, but don't do it again.
...Oh yes, we were talking about what they did with the painting.{p}

The painting had gone back to her house.
What's more, it was lying on the bed in her room.
And of course, nobody had carried it there.
Her family must have been shocked.
But there was something even more startling to come.{p}

That portrait, hanging in the very same spot as before.
It caused an uproar.
But once school let out, the painting disappeared again.{p}

From then on, the painting came to school every day.
But it wasn't doing any harm, so they decided to let it do as it pleased.
That was what Shimizu's family wanted, too.
Then, one day, after several months had gone by...
Something terrible happened.{p}What do you think it was?
Her house caught fire
Her family was in a car accident

In the middle of the night one day, her house caught fire.
Her family escaped unharmed, but the house burned to the ground.
Naturally, the painting that had been on her bed burned with it.
The Shimizus, burned out of their home, moved away, saying they would go to stay with relatives.{p}

But some time after that, the portrait appeared in the art room once again.
Even though the fire had been so fierce that nothing should have been left.
I suppose that just shows how strong the feelings Shimizu left in that painting were.
But, you see, there was one problem.
Her house had burned down.
And her family had moved far away, hadn't they?
...That's right. The painting no longer had a home to go back to.{p}
After that, the painting stopped disappearing at night.

Instead, a rumor started that it would begin sobbing late at night.
She must have been lonely, I'm sure.
But everyone was so frightened of it that in the end they took the painting down.

And it was settled that the art club would keep it in storage.
After that, nothing else ever happened.{p}

...Heh heh, do you see now?
The reason I wanted to bring that painting out was to give her a chance to look for her family. If I'm right, that painting will go off in search of them.
Say, let's go and take a look.
You'll come with me, won't you?{p}

...But it's exciting, isn't it?
We might even catch the painting in the act of moving.
Doesn't it make your heart pound?
All right, I'm opening the door.{p}

...Look, {a}{f:|}!
The painting's still hanging there, but......the person in it is gone★
It isn't a different painting.
I remember seeing that faint stain in the corner earlier.
Only the figure has slipped out of the portrait!
I never imagined this would happen...{p}

But I wonder what she looks like, now that she's left the painting.
Is she as flat and thin as paper?
Or is she only the upper half that was painted?
Is she even still in Shimizu's shape at all?
Heh heh, what do you think, {a}{f:|}?
It didn't turn out the way I expected, but that's the end of my story.
Let's go back to the club room and hear the next one.{p}

The car her family was riding in went off a cliff, from brake failure or something.
They say every one of them died instantly.{p}

After the funeral, one of their relatives, an uncle, moved into the Shimizu house.
And he couldn't stand her painting, so he announced he was going to donate it to the school.{p}

The school accepted it, but...
maybe that was where things went wrong.{p}

One day, her painting, which should have been in the art room, suddenly vanished.
Everyone searched, but they couldn't find it, so they decided to ask the relative, just in case.{p}

But again, there was no answer.
And yet, they could hear what sounded like a TV inside.
Thinking he was pretending not to be home, they turned the doorknob, and sure enough, it wasn't locked.
So they opened the door, they say.{p}

A large animal... can you picture anything?
I can.
Because that portrait was lying right there at the scene.
If I told you there was something like blood around her mouth in that painting... would you believe me?
To Shimizu, it was as good as having her own home stolen from her.
No, maybe even her family's accident wasn't just an accident.{p}

...Heh heh, what a frightened face, {a}{f:|}.
Did you take my wild guesswork seriously?
The blood on the painting might just have spattered onto it, you know.
The truth lies in darkness, after all... heh heh.
And with that, I'll end my story.
Who's next?{p}

That's right, the painting was in the club room.
A boy from the art club had taken it there.
Why would he do that, you ask?
Because he was in love with Shimizu.
So he wanted the portrait that Shimizu had clung to even after her death.
That's when the real trouble started.

The boy wouldn't leave Shimizu's painting.
Not when the teachers scolded him, not even when night fell.
In the end, his family came and tried to talk him round.
But he wouldn't listen.
He stayed rooted to the spot, they say, just staring and staring at the painting.
So there was nothing for it but to move the painting instead.
If they took it home, at least the boy would follow it.
And that's exactly what happened.{p}

Led by his family, who carried the painting in their arms, the boy staggered home.
And after that, he never came to school again.{p}

Apparently he sat in his room staring at the painting, never moving at all.
Not eating, not sleeping, just staring, on and on.
That went on for nearly a month.
His family was so worried they even tried to take him to the hospital.
But whenever they tried to pull him away from the painting, he went berserk, they say.
With a strength you'd never think a human could have.{p}

As a last resort, the family called in a counselor.
But it was a little too late.
When the counselor went into his room, he had already stopped breathing.
He had wasted away and died.{p}

But strangely, even then he was still sitting there, gazing up at the painting hung on the wall.
When they tried to move him, it was as if he had turned to stone; they couldn't even change his pose.
After his funeral, the portrait was returned to the school.
But nobody would go near it anymore.
After all, it holds the feelings of two people now.
If you got close to it, you might be bewitched just like he was.
That's the kind of history that painting has.{p}

...Oh my, you look rather angry.
Is it because I invited you to the art room, where that painting is, without telling you any of this?
Heh heh... Aren't you getting scared now, a little too late?
Well then, I'll end my story here.
Who's next?{p}

The painting was in front of her grave.
And a man was lying collapsed there.
A stranger nobody recognized, wearing a filthy windbreaker.
By the time he was found, he was already dead.
The cause of death was heart failure, they say.{p}

Why a man like that died at her grave, no one knows.
But maybe... he was the one who killed Shimizu, don't you think?
The portrait took its revenge... that's a little hard to believe, isn't it?
But that's how it seems to me.
After that, Shimizu's ghost never appeared again, and the painting never disappeared again.
Which makes me feel that way all the more.{p}

But it's amazing, isn't it?
To be able to take revenge that way.

Oh, no you don't.
After listening this far, you can't back out now, can you?
Come on, stand up.
You're coming.
If you don't come, I won't forgive you.
Come on!{p}

Oh, are you really sure?
Haven't you noticed the eerie presence drifting through this room?
And you'd stay behind alone in a place like this?
...Well, if that's what you want, I don't mind.
But you're a strange one.
I'd never do it, not for anything.
Well then, we're going, but if you change your mind, come after us.{p}

Everyone except {f:me|me} stood up and began filing out of the room.
Iwashita, the last to go, looked back at {f:me|me}.{p}
"Be careful..."

She giggled softly.
A chill ran down my spine.
{f:Did she know something?|Did she know something?}
Suddenly, the thought of being left alone in this room scared me.

The door closed.
Alone now, the club room, which should have been cramped, felt strangely vast.
It seemed as if something might be lurking in the dim corners of the room, and {f:I|I} couldn't help glancing all around.
Just then, there was a small clack.{p}

I whirled around.
...No one was there.{p}

My eyes met those of the girl in the painting.
The girl's mouth moved.
D... i... e......

Die★
Stunned, {f:I|I} watched my hands rise on their own, against my will.
{f:My|My} hands were trying to strangle {f:me|me}?
I couldn't believe it.

But the force crushing my throat was real, and the pain made me start to black out.
My knees gave way, and {f:I|I} collapsed to the floor.
But my hands wouldn't let me go.
They squeezed tighter and tighter.
I couldn't breathe anymore.{p}
As my vision grew darker and darker, I saw the girl in the portrait smirk......{p}

{a}{f:|}, you really do have sick taste.
Are you that eager to see that face?{p}
All right, then let's open it.{p}
Can you see the face you were hoping for?{p}

To me it's just an ordinary painting, but I wonder what it looks like to you.
Maybe you're seeing the face she had when she was killed.
If so, {a}{f:|}, you might just be the fifth one, don't you think?
...I'm a little curious about the face you saw, but I think I'll not ask after all.
You may not believe it, but I scare easily.{p}
...It's gone. The painting★{p}
Did someone take it back to the art club's room?{p}

...No, it doesn't seem to be here either.
I'm amazed. What you said, {a}{f:|}, actually came true.{p}

Are you some kind of psychic?
Heh heh... I'm starting to find you rather interesting.
Well then, shall we go back?
We have to hear the fourth story.
What, where the painting went?
I don't know.
But what does that matter?
This project is about telling the seven wonders, isn't it?
If everything were explained, they wouldn't be wonders at all, would they?
Am I wrong?
...Come on, let's go on... heh heh.{p}

What's with that careless attitude?
I'm asking you something, so would you answer me properly?{p}
I'll ask you once more.{p}{a}{f:|}, what do you want to have happened to the portrait?
The painting is unchanged, just as it was
It has the face she had when she was killed
The painting is gone from the art room
